channel.title: Gateway Studio KH
channel.description: The newest Gateway Studio KH for Macs that already have it.

item.title: Version 0.2.308
item.description: - **API keys now rotate with a 24-hour overlap instead of cutting off sleeping Macs.** Settings now offers **Rotate** in place of Regenerate: pressing it writes a new key and restarts the Gateway so the new key works immediately, while the previous key keeps working across `/v1`, `/v1/content`, and admin routes until the expiry time shown in Settings (24 hours from the press). Unrelated `.env` entries are preserved, and a key inherited from the launch environment is refused plainly instead of pretending to rotate. - **Hidden background launches stay windowless across relaunch.** The menu-bar app now honours `GATEWAY_BACKGROUND=1` alongside `--background` so background and self-update verification launches stay windowless and Dock-less.

item.title: Version 0.2.307
item.description: - **Every place a job was passed over now says why, where the job waits.** The Jobs view lists each site the Gateway tried and the reason it declined — busy, no such model, drained — instead of only naming the machine that failed. - **The first look at a sleeping Mac is no longer mistaken for an outage.** After a quiet spell a site gets the full 20-second window instead of ten, so a Mac that was asleep stops reading as unreachable and the fleet count stops collapsing to whichever sites happened to be awake.

item.title: Version 0.2.306
item.description: - **Updates can hold your work again, and stop borrowing the shared token file.** Gateway now keeps its own hold token in its own folder, copying the shared one across once the first time it starts; the old shared file is never read again. When the token cannot be read, the app says so on screen in plain words instead of quietly refusing every update.

item.title: Version 0.2.305
item.description: - **Gateway can now update itself, and it holds your work first.** The app checks a signed feed in the background and installs a new version without a window, a prompt or a click. Before it fetches anything it puts its own work on hold through the same maintenance hold an install already uses, so no running job is cut off; if the hold cannot be taken, the update is refused instead of forced. Work resumes by itself when the check finishes. - **Gateway now requires macOS 12 or later.** The updater's library is built for it.
